source_text:
γάλακτι ἐπιχριόμενος τοῖς εἱλκωμένοις τόποις. Καὶ ἡ ἐν τῷ ὄρει δὲ τῷ Μωϋσῇ
δοθεῖσα νομοθεσία, ἐπὶ λίθῳ σαπφείρῳ λέγεται πεφηνέναι. Ἰάσπις σμαραγδίζων μέν
ἐστιν, εὑρίσκεται δὲ παρὰ τὸ στόμα Μερμόδοντος τοῦ ποταμοῦ, καὶ παρὰἈμαθουντίῳ
Κύπρου. Χρησιμεύει δὲ εἰς τὰς ἐπιλήψεις. Ὑάκινθος ὑποπυρίζων μέν ἐστιν,
εὑρίσκεται δὲ ἐν τῇ ἐσωτέρᾳ Βαρβαρίᾳ τῆς Σκυθίας. Σκυθίαν δὲ εἰώθασι καλεῖν οἱ
παλαιοὶ τὸ κλίμα ἅπαν τὸ βόρειον, ἔνθα εἰσὶν οἱ Γότθοι καὶ ∆άνεις.Ἐκεῖ τοίνυν
ἔνδον ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τῆς μεγάλης Σκυθίας ἐστὶ φάραγξ λίαν βαθυτάτη, καὶ ἀνθρώποις
ἄβατος, ὄρεσι πετρῶν ἐντεῦθεν καὶ ἐντεῦθεν περιστοιχισμένη, ὥστε ἄνωθεν ἀπ'
ἄκρων τῶν ὀρέων παρακύψαντά τινα, ὡς ἀπὸ τειχῶν, μὴ δύνασθαι κατοπτεύειν τὸ
ἔδαφος τῆς φάραγγος, ἀλλ' ἀπὸ τοῦ βάθους ἐσκοτίσθαι ὥσπερ τι χάος· ἐν ᾗ οἱ
ἀπεσταλμένοι ἀπὸ τῶν ἐκεῖσε πλη89.589 σιαζόντων βασιλέων, κατάδικοί εἰσι καὶ
βιαζόμενοι. Θύσαντες δὲ ἀρνοὺς καὶ ἐκδείραντες ῥίπτουσιν ἄνωθεν ἀπὸ τῶν πετρῶν
εἰς τὸ χάος τῆς φάραγγος, καὶ κολλῶσιν οἱ λίθοι ἐν τοῖς κρέασιν ἐκείνοις. Ἀετοὶ οὖν
ἐν ταῖς πέτραις ἄνωθεν κατοικοῦντες, πρὸς τὴν ὀσμὴν τῶν κρεῶν κατέρχονται, καὶ
ἀναφέρουσι τοὺς ἀρνοὺς ἔχοντας τοὺς λίθους.Ἐν δὲ τῷ ἐσθίειν τὰ κρέα οἱ λίθοι
μένουσιν ἐν τῇ ἀκρωρείᾳ τῶν ὀρέων.
thought_title: Sapphire lawgiving, jasper, and the Scythian ravine hyacinth
orientation: Epiphanius continues his catalogue of the twelve stones, moving from the sapphire's healing use to the lawgiving on a sapphire stone, then to jasper and the legendary Scythian ravine where the hyacinth is found.
pass_a_gloss: with milk being smeared on the ulcerated places. And the giving of the law that was given to Moses on the mountain is said to have appeared on a sapphire stone. Jasper is greenish, and it is found near the mouth of the river Mermodon, and near Amathus in Cyprus. And it is useful for epileptic seizures. Hyacinth is somewhat fiery-red, and it is found in inner Barbaria of Scythia. And the ancients are accustomed to call the whole northern region Scythia, where the Goths and Danes are. There, then, inside in the desert of great Scythia there is a ravine exceedingly deep, and inaccessible to humans, surrounded on this side and that side by crags of rocks, so that someone peering down from above from the tops of the mountains, as from walls, is not able to observe the floor of the ravine, but from the depth it is darkened like some chaos; in which the condemned men sent from the kings dwelling near there are, and they are forced. And having sacrificed lambs and having flayed them, they throw them down from above from the rocks into the chaos of the ravine, and the stones stick to those meats. Eagles, then, dwelling above in the rocks, come down toward the smell of the meats, and they carry up the lambs having the stones. And while the meats are being eaten, the stones remain on the summit of the mountains.

choices.why: Glossary term for the lawgiving to Moses on Sinai; kept as required.
The verb means 'to be emerald-like' in color; 'greenish' conveys the color sense without implying it is emerald itself.
The prefix hypo- indicates a lesser degree; 'somewhat fiery-red' captures the partial redness.
The source uses the word for a dark, formless depth; keeping 'chaos' preserves the vivid image of the ravine's darkness.
The term refers to those sentenced to punishment; 'condemned men' is literal and clear.
The word means the topmost part of a mountain; 'summit' is the natural English equivalent.

pass_b_english: smeared on the ulcerated places with milk. And the giving of the law on the mountain to Moses is said to have appeared on a sapphire stone. Iaspis is greenish, and it is found at the mouth of the river Mermodon and near Amathus in Cyprus. It is useful for epileptic seizures. Hyacinth is somewhat fiery-red, and it is found in inner Scythia, the barbarian land. The ancients used to call the whole northern region Scythia, where the Goths and Danes are. There, deep within the desert of great Scythia, is a ravine of immense depth, inaccessible to human beings, walled in on both sides by crags of rock, so that if someone leans over from the top of the mountains, as from a wall, he cannot see the floor of the ravine, but from its depth it is darkened like a chaos. In this ravine are condemned men sent by the kings who live nearby, and they are forced to work there. They slaughter lambs, skin them, and throw them down from the rocks above into the chaos of the ravine, and the stones stick to that meat. Then eagles that live on the rocks above come down at the smell of the meat and carry up the lambs with the stones. But while they eat the meat, the stones remain on the summit of the mountains.
notes: The source text contains 'πλη89.589' which appears to be OCR damage or a stray numeral; it has been omitted from the gloss as it does not form part of the Greek text.

problems.why: ἐσωτέρᾳ is feminine dative modifying Scythia, not 'barbarian land'; means 'inner/remote Scythia'
problems.ruling: ἐσωτέρᾳ Βαρβαρίᾳ = inner Barbaria; 'inner barbarian land' misreads as generic descriptor, not proper name

edits.old: in the inner barbarian land of Scythia
edits.new: in inner Scythia, the barbarian land

fixed: Changed 'inner barbarian land of Scythia' to 'inner Scythia, the barbarian land' because ἐσωτέρᾳ is feminine dative modifying Σκυθίας, not Βαρβαρίᾳ.

last_rejected.why: English adds 'the barbarian land' as apposition, but source has 'inner Scythia' as genitive dependent on 'Barbaria'
last_rejected.ruling: ἐσωτέρᾳ Βαρβαρίᾳ τῆς Σκυθίας: 'inner Barbaria of Scythia'; 'barbarian land' paraphrases Βαρβαρίᾳ adequately

last_rejected.quote: condemned men sent by the kings who live nearby, and they are forced to work there
last_rejected.why: βιαζόμενοι means 'forced men/compelled laborers', not 'forced to work there' as a separate clause; English makes it passive rather than substantive
last_rejected.fix: are condemned men and forced laborers sent by the neighboring kings
last_rejected.ruling: κατάδικοί εἰσι καὶ βιαζόμενοι: 'condemned men and forced laborers'; 'forced to work there' captures βιαζόμενοι adequately

last_rejected.why: The ravine was just called inaccessible to humans, and the men throw lambs down from above; ἐν ᾗ refers to the desert or region, not inside the ravine.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐν ᾗ naturally refers to φάραγξ; ἄβατος targets the floor, while κατάδικοι act ἄνωθεν from the cliffs.
